current_direction_basis: Driven by the 2025-2026 evidence collected here, not by her (older) research.html narrative. (1) The Science 2026 paper 'A statistical test for the benefits of personalizing interventions' (Li & Brunskill, 2026-07-09) is a two-author paper with a current postdoc and is the clearest signal of the personalization-testing thrust. (2) 'Efficient RL for optimizing conversation level outcomes with an LLM-based tutor' (2025-07-22, NeurIPS 2025 workshop) plus 'Repairing Reward Functions with Feedback to Mitigate Reward Hacking' (2025-10-14) show RL now being applied on top of LLM systems. (3) PNAS 2026 'Computer-assisted learning in the real world: How Khan Academy influences student math learning', 'Assessing the Quality of AI-Generated Exams: A Large-Scale Field Study' (AAAI 2026) and 'The GPT Surprise' (L@S 2025) are all large-scale real-world field evaluations. (4) Two CHI 2026 papers ('Bloom: Designing for LLM-Augmented Behavior Change Interactions' and 'Can LLM-Simulated Practice and Feedback Upskill Human Counselors?') plus SYNAPSE (2026-08-07) show the LLM-simulation / behavior-change line. (5) 'Active Learning for Stochastic Contextual Linear Bandits' (AISTATS 2026, with current lab members Karmarkar and Li) and 'Cost-Aware Near-Optimal Policy Learning' (AAAI 2025) carry the theory line forward.

OPENING -- UPHELD under a second, independent adversarial re-verification on 2026-08-31. Every claim below was fetched fresh in that pass; nothing is carried on trust from the prior harvest.

STEP 1 (the load-bearing check). https://cs.stanford.edu/people/ebrun/students.html returns HTTP 200 with Last-Modified Thu, 02 Jul 2026 18:06:23 GMT. The final paragraph of the page body reads, verbatim: "If you're an undergraduate or graduate already enrolled at Stanford interested in helping us transform and scale personalized learning, or tackling new challenges in sequential decision making under uncertainty, please get in touch!" An exact fixed-string grep for that whole sentence against the freshly downloaded HTML returns exactly one match, so this is page text, not a reconstruction. It clears both bars the check demands: (a) present tense with a direct imperative ask, no past tense, no 'previously', no closed or filled language anywhere on the page; and (b) undergraduate-relevant by its own first word of address -- it literally says 'undergraduate', so it is not a PhD-applicant notice being stretched to cover undergrads. The page was touched about two months before this check, and that same edit refreshed the alumni roster, so this is live text on a maintained page rather than a fossil.

THE OBVIOUS COUNTERARGUMENT, CHECKED AND REJECTED. The site does carry discouraging recruiting language: the homepage says 'Unfortunately I generally won't be able to talk to prospective students until after admissions decisions have been made.' That sentence is explicitly scoped -- its own heading is 'Prospective PhD student applicants' and it concerns people not yet admitted. The group-page invitation is scoped to people 'already enrolled at Stanford'. The two address disjoint audiences, so the homepage note does not close the undergraduate door and should not be quoted to a Stanford student as a reason not to write.

WHAT THIS OPENING IS NOT -- read this before recommending 'apply now'. There is no application form, no deadline, no stipend or funding statement, no slot count, and no named program. A grep for 'CURIS' and for the word 'REU' across all seven lab HTML pages returns zero hits on every page. This is a standing open-door invitation to email her, backed by the CS 195 / CS 191W / CS 199 / CS 199P independent-study vehicles she is listed to supervise for 2025-26 on Stanford Profiles (all four strings verified literally on a fresh fetch, links carrying academicYear=20252026). Being listed to supervise those numbers is authorization, not proof of a free slot. The honest action for a student is a well-targeted cold email, not an application to a posted position.

ELIGIBILITY CAVEAT, LOAD-BEARING. The invitation's own wording limits it to students 'already enrolled at Stanford'. A current Stanford undergraduate is squarely inside it. A non-Stanford undergraduate is outside its wording, is also outside the PhD-applicant note, and has no statement on this site inviting them -- for that reader this lab is WATCH, not an opening.

LAB ACTIVITY (re-confirmed this pass). publications.html (HTTP 200, Last-Modified 27 Feb 2026) carries a '2026' heading followed by 'Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS) 2026', 'Association for the Advancement of AI (AAAI) Conference 2026' and two 'Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI) 2026' entries, and the group page lists three current post-docs and four current Ph.D. students. The lab is unambiguously active.

CONTACT CAVEAT. email and email_source_url are null and stay null: the literal string 'ebrun@cs.stanford.edu' does not appear on its recorded source page or on any other fetched page. The only address-like text on publications.html is the deliberately obfuscated 'email me at ebrun AT cs dot stanford dot edu', quoted in fetch_notes for a human to de-obfuscate. A student acting on this opening should use that sentence or the Stanford Profiles contact route, not a value from this record.

CONFIDENCE 0.85, and the 0.15 is not doubt about the sentence -- that is certain. It is doubt about whether a standing, undated, unfunded open-door invitation converts into an actual undergraduate position on any given month.
